name: Cherokee Purple
description: Famously rich flavor and texture make this a colorful favorite among heirloom enthusiasts. Medium-large, flattened globe, 8-12 oz. fruits. Color is dusky pink with dark shoulders. Multilocular interior ranges from purple to brown to green. Relatively short vines. Indeterminate.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained loam with plenty of organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost date. Transplant after all danger of frost has passed and soil is at least 60°F.
flavor_profile: Rich, sweet, and smoky with complex earthy undertones
culinary_uses: Fresh slicing, sandwiches, salads, BLTs. Not ideal for canning due to low acidity.
disease_resistance: Limited disease resistance typical of heirlooms. Susceptible to late blight and cracking.
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, whiteflies, flea beetles
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, fusarium wilt, blossom end rot

name: Better Boy
description: One of the most popular hybrid tomatoes for good reason - this reliable performer produces heavy yields of large, flavorful fruits with excellent disease resistance. Perfect for beginner gardeners who want guaranteed success and experienced growers who appreciate consistent performance. The classic red slicing tomato that delivers on both quantity and quality.
soil_type: Well-drained garden soil with moderate organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost date. Transplant outdoors when soil temperature reaches 60°F.
flavor_profile: Balanced sweet-tart flavor with classic tomato taste
culinary_uses: Versatile for slicing, sandwiches, salads, cooking, and canning
disease_resistance: Excellent resistance to Verticillium wilt, Fusarium wilt, and Nematodes (VFN)
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, cutworms, aphids
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, bacterial spot

name: San Marzano
description: San Marzano tomatoes are a heritage Italian plum variety prized for sauce production. These elongated, deep red fruits mature in approximately 60 days and feature distinctly few seeds and thin walls—ideal characteristics for canning and paste-making. Known for their sweet flavor profile with notably low acidity and intense, concentrated tomato taste, San Marzanos are the traditional choice for authentic Italian sauces. While classified as hybrid here, true San Marzano varieties are often open-pollinated heirlooms. The plants require full sun and rich, well-drained soil, with moderate to difficult cultivation demands.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with high organic matter content
sowing_method: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Requires warm soil (65°F+) for transplanting.
flavor_profile: Sweet with low acidity, intense tomato flavor, minimal seeds
culinary_uses: Premium sauce making, paste, canning, pizza sauce, marinara
disease_resistance: Early Blight (Intermediate); Late Blight (Intermediate)
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, spider mites, whiteflies
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, fusarium wilt, bacterial canker

name: Celebrity
description: Celebrity is a classic hybrid tomato that matures in 60 days, producing large, deep red, globe-shaped fruits ideal for slicing and general-purpose use. Known for its dependable yields and disease resistance, Celebrity has been a home gardener favorite for decades. The fruit offers a well-balanced, classic tomato flavor with pleasant acidity, making it excellent for fresh eating, salads, and cooking. Its vigorous plant habit and consistent performance in full sun conditions make it a reliable choice for both beginners and experienced growers seeking tried-and-true productivity.
soil_type: Well-drained garden soil, adapts to various soil types
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Transplant after soil warms to 60°F.
flavor_profile: Well-balanced, classic tomato flavor with good acidity
culinary_uses: Excellent for slicing, salads, sandwiches, and general cooking
disease_resistance: Early Blight (Intermediate); Late Blight (Intermediate)
common_pests: Hornworms, cutworms, flea beetles
common_diseases: Late blight, bacterial spot, blossom end rot

name: Brandywine
description: We describe Brandywine's luscious, heirloom flavor as "very rich, loud, and distinctively spicy." The large fruits, often over 1 lb., have a deep pink skin and smooth red flesh. The medium-tall, potato-leaf plant is best staked or caged. Our 'Quisenberry' strain is considered among the best. Indeterminate.
soil_type: Rich, deep, well-drained soil with abundant organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Requires strong support system due to large fruit size.
color: Pink to rose-pink with some yellow shoulders
flavor_profile: Intensely sweet, rich, and complex with perfect acid balance
culinary_uses: Premium fresh eating, slicing for special occasions, not suitable for canning
disease_resistance: Very limited disease resistance, requires preventive care
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, spider mites, cutworms
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, fusarium wilt, cracking, blossom end rot

name: Roma
description: Roma is a classic heirloom paste tomato prized for its dense, meaty flesh and concentrated flavor. The plant produces elongated, plum-shaped fruits that mature in 60-65 days with minimal seeds and low acidity. Known for its mild, sweet taste, Roma excels in fresh sauces, pastes, and cooking applications where robust texture matters. This reliable, easy-to-grow variety tolerates less fertile soil and requires minimal maintenance. Its naturally rich flavor develops without excessive acidity, making it ideal for traditional Italian tomato preparations.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Well-drained soil, tolerates less fertile conditions
sowing_method: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost date. Direct sow in warm climates when soil reaches 65°F.
flavor_profile: Concentrated, less acidic, mild and sweet
culinary_uses: Ideal for sauces, paste, canning, drying, and cooking. Can be eaten fresh but bred for processing.
disease_resistance: Moderate resistance to common tomato diseases. Less susceptible to cracking than slicing varieties.
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, whiteflies
common_diseases: Early blight, late blight, fusarium wilt

name: Cherry Belle
description: A prolific cherry tomato that produces hundreds of sweet, bite-sized fruits throughout the growing season. These vigorous indeterminate plants are perfect for snacking straight from the garden and add color to salads and appetizers. Kids love picking and eating these candy-like tomatoes right off the vine.
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with good organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Can direct sow in warm climates 2-3 weeks after last frost date.
flavor_profile: Very sweet with bright, intense tomato flavor and slight tartness
culinary_uses: Perfect for snacking, salads, garnishes, roasting whole, and preserving. Great for kids' gardens.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to cracking and splitting. Moderate disease resistance typical of cherry varieties.
common_pests: Birds, tomato hornworm, aphids, spider mites
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, powdery mildew

name: Early Girl
description: A longtime early favorite, Early Girl produces heavy yields of full-flavored, 4-6 oz. tomatoes. One of the first varieties to ripen each year. Also prized for its performance as a "dry-farmed" tomato, owing to its extreme tolerance to drought and blossom end rot. Indeterminate.
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Transplant when soil reaches 60°F and night temperatures stay above 50°F.
flavor_profile: Well-balanced sweet-tart flavor with good acidity
culinary_uses: Excellent for slicing, sandwiches, salads, and general cooking. Good for canning and sauces.
disease_resistance: Fusarium Wilt races 1, 2 (High); Verticillium Wilt (High)
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, cutworms, spider mites
common_diseases: Early blight, late blight, bacterial speck, blossom end rot

name: Big Beef
description: Still unsurpassed as the top choice for fresh market beefsteak tomatoes. Large, avg. 10-12 oz., mostly blemish-free, globe-shaped red fruit. They have full flavor - among the best - and ripen early for their size. Broad disease resistance package. AAS Winner. Indeterminate.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained loam with high organic content
sowing_method: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost date. Transplant outdoors when soil temperature reaches 65°F.
color: Deep red with slight pink undertones
flavor_profile: Rich, full-bodied tomato flavor with perfect sweet-acid balance
culinary_uses: Premium slicing tomato for sandwiches and fresh eating. Excellent for stuffing and grilling.
disease_resistance: Alternaria Stem Canker (High); Fusarium Wilt races 1, 2 (High); Gray Leaf Spot (High); Nematodes (High); Tobacco Mosaic Virus (High); Verticillium Wilt (High)
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, whiteflies, spider mites
common_diseases: Late blight, bacterial spot, septoria leaf spot

name: Green Zebra
description: A delicious, tangy salad tomato, ripe just as the green fruit develops a yellow blush, accentuating the darker green stripes. The 3-4 oz. fruits are the ideal size for slicing into wedges for salads. Productive over a long season. Developed by Tom Wagner. Indeterminate.
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with organic matter
sowing_method: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Transplant when nighttime temperatures stay above 55°F.
color: Green with dark green stripes, yellow undertones when ripe
flavor_profile: Tangy, zesty, and tart with bright acidity and citrus notes
culinary_uses: Excellent for fresh eating, salads, salsas, and garnishes. Creates stunning fried green tomatoes.
disease_resistance: Moderate disease resistance, better than most heirlooms. Some resistance to cracking.
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, whiteflies, spider mites
common_diseases: Early blight, late blight, fusarium wilt, bacterial speck

name: Beefsteak
description: The classic giant of the tomato world, producing massive fruits that can weigh over a pound each. These impressive slicing tomatoes have been a garden favorite for generations, offering substantial, meaty slices perfect for sandwiches and burgers. Their size and reliable production make them a must-have for gardeners who want to impress with truly spectacular harvests.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained loam with high organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Transplant when soil reaches 65°F and nighttime temps stay above 55°F.
shape: Large, round to slightly flattened, ribbed
flavor_profile: Mild, sweet, and balanced with low acidity
culinary_uses: Premium slicing for sandwiches, burgers, fresh eating. Excellent stuffed. Too large for most canning.
disease_resistance: Limited resistance; requires good garden hygiene and air circulation
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, spider mites, cutworms
common_diseases: Blossom end rot, cracking, late blight, fusarium wilt

name: Mortgage Lifter
description: This legendary heirloom tomato earned its name when creator M.C. Byles paid off his mortgage by selling seedlings for $1 each during the Depression. These massive pink beefsteak tomatoes can weigh up to 4 pounds and offer exceptional flavor with meaty texture and few seeds. Perfect for gardeners who want to grow truly impressive conversation-starter tomatoes.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with plenty of compost
sowing_method: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost date. Transplant when soil is consistently above 60°F.
shape: Large beefsteak, slightly flattened with moderate ribbing
flavor_profile: Sweet and rich with perfect balance, minimal acidity
culinary_uses: Premium fresh slicing, sandwiches, salads. Single slice can cover an entire sandwich. Not suitable for canning.
disease_resistance: Typical heirloom susceptibility; good air circulation essential
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, spider mites, whiteflies
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, blossom end rot, cracking in wet weather

name: Stupice
description: This Czechoslovakian heirloom is prized as one of the earliest full-flavored tomatoes, often ripening weeks before other varieties. Despite its early maturity, it delivers complex, rich flavor that rivals the best season tomatoes. Perfect for short-season gardeners who don't want to sacrifice taste for earliness.
soil_type: Well-drained loam, adaptable to various soil types
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Can tolerate cooler transplant conditions than most varieties.
flavor_profile: Rich, complex flavor with good balance of sweet and tart
culinary_uses: Excellent fresh eating, salads, sandwiches. Good for sauce and canning due to balanced flavor.
disease_resistance: Good cold tolerance, moderate disease resistance for an heirloom
common_pests: Aphids, spider mites, tomato hornworm
common_diseases: Early blight, late blight, but generally more resistant than many heirlooms

name: Black Krim
description: Black Krim combines bold, smoky flavor and good texture with an unusual appearance. Deep brown/red, 8-16 oz. tomatoes have brown/green shoulders that get darker with more heat and sunlight. High-yielding. Indeterminate.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with good organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Transplant after soil warms to 65°F.
flavor_profile: Rich, complex, and smoky with sweet undertones and mild saltiness
culinary_uses: Gourmet fresh slicing, specialty salads, farmers market sales. Beautiful contrast in dishes. Low acid - not ideal for canning.
disease_resistance: Typical heirloom susceptibility, prone to cracking in wet conditions
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, whiteflies, spider mites
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, blossom end rot, fruit cracking

name: Yellow Pear
description: A charming heirloom cherry tomato dating back to the 1800s, producing abundant clusters of bright yellow, pear-shaped fruits that are as decorative as they are delicious. This prolific variety is beloved by children and adults alike for its sweet, mild flavor and unique teardrop shape that adds visual interest to any garden or salad.
soil_type: Well-drained garden soil, adaptable
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost or direct sow after last frost date when soil is warm.
flavor_profile: Sweet and mild with low acidity, fruity undertones
culinary_uses: Fresh snacking, salads, garnishes, children's gardens. Beautiful in mixed dishes. Can be used for unique yellow preserves.
disease_resistance: Generally hardy with good disease tolerance for an heirloom
common_pests: Aphids, whiteflies, spider mites, birds (love the sweet fruit)
common_diseases: Early blight, late blight, minimal cracking due to small size

name: Rutgers
description: A legendary heirloom variety developed at Rutgers University in 1934 that became the standard for tomato flavor in America. This reliable producer delivers perfectly balanced, old-fashioned tomato taste in medium-sized fruits that are ideal for both fresh eating and processing. Rutgers represents the classic American tomato that many gardeners remember from their childhood.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained loam with plenty of organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost date. Transplant after all danger of frost has passed and soil is at least 60°F.
flavor_profile: Classic balanced tomato flavor with good acidity and sweetness
culinary_uses: Excellent for fresh eating, slicing, canning, sauces, and paste. Perfect all-purpose tomato.
disease_resistance: Good overall disease resistance for an heirloom variety
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, whiteflies, cutworms
common_diseases: Early blight, late blight, fusarium wilt, bacterial spot

name: Patio Princess
description: Specially bred for container growing, Patio Princess produces full-sized tomatoes on compact, sturdy plants that thrive in pots and small spaces. Despite its diminutive size, this determinate variety delivers surprising yields of 4-6 oz red tomatoes with excellent flavor. Perfect for urban gardeners, balcony growers, and anyone wanting fresh tomatoes without a large garden space.
soil_type: Well-drained potting mix with good organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost or direct seed when soil temperature reaches 65°F. Ideal for 5+ gallon containers.
flavor_profile: Sweet and tangy with good tomato flavor for a compact variety
culinary_uses: Fresh slicing, salads, sandwiches, snacking. Good for small-batch cooking.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to verticillium wilt and fusarium wilt (VF)
common_pests: Aphids, spider mites, whiteflies, thrips
common_diseases: Early blight, blossom end rot, bacterial speck

name: Amish Paste
description: Large for a sauce tomato, Amish Paste's slightly irregular plum to strawberry-shaped fruits avg. 8-12 oz. with excellent flavor. These meaty tomatoes are good in salads and great for processing. A Slow Food USA Ark of Taste variety. Indeterminate.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained loam with plenty of organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost date. Transplant after all danger of frost has passed and soil is at least 60°F.
flavor_profile: Rich, sweet, and intense with low acidity - excellent concentrated tomato flavor
culinary_uses: Outstanding for sauces, paste, canning, and cooking. Good fresh eating despite being a paste type.
disease_resistance: Limited disease resistance typical of heirlooms. Some tolerance to cracking.
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, flea beetles, stink bugs
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, fusarium wilt, bacterial canker

name: Mountain Fresh Plus
description: Able to tolerate cool and wet conditions, this big red tomato produces attractive, 8-16 oz. slicers with good flavor. Developed by Dr. Randy Gardner at North Carolina State University. Vigorous plants provide plenty of leaf cover. Determinate.
soil_type: Well-drained loam with good organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost date. Transplant after all danger of frost has passed and soil is at least 60°F.
flavor_profile: Excellent balance of sweetness and acidity with rich tomato flavor
culinary_uses: Premium fresh eating, slicing, salads. Good for light cooking and fresh salsas.
disease_resistance: Fusarium Wilt races 1, 2 (High); Nematodes (High); Verticillium Wilt (High)
common_pests: Tomato hornworm, aphids, spider mites, thrips
common_diseases: Bacterial speck, blossom end rot (with inconsistent watering)

name: Surefire Red
description: An All-America Selections winner bred specifically for cool-weather performance and short growing seasons, producing ripe tomatoes even when temperatures dip below ideal ranges. This compact hybrid sets fruit reliably in conditions that cause other varieties to drop blossoms, making it perfect for northern gardens and unpredictable climates. Surefire Red delivers dependable harvests when gardening success seems uncertain.
soil_type: Well-drained garden soil with moderate fertility
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Can be planted earlier than most tomatoes. Good for succession planting.
flavor_profile: Good balanced flavor with pleasant sweetness and mild acidity
culinary_uses: Excellent for fresh eating, salads, sandwiches, and light cooking. Perfect for beginning gardeners.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to verticillium wilt, fusarium wilt, and tobacco mosaic virus (VFT)
common_pests: Aphids, cutworms, flea beetles, whiteflies
common_diseases: Early blight, late blight, bacterial spot

name: Bell Pepper 'California Wonder'
description: The gold standard for sweet bell peppers, California Wonder has been America's favorite home garden variety since the 1920s. These thick-walled, blocky peppers start green and can ripen to brilliant red, offering exceptional sweetness and crunch. Reliable, productive, and perfect for beginners, it's the pepper that built America's love affair with home-grown sweet peppers.
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile loam with good organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Transplant when soil temperature reaches 65°F and nighttime temperatures stay above 55°F.
shape: Blocky, square-shouldered bell shape with 3-4 lobes
flavor_profile: Sweet, mild, and crisp with no heat
culinary_uses: Fresh eating, stuffing, roasting, grilling, stir-fries, salads, and preserving
disease_resistance: Moderate resistance to tobacco mosaic virus
common_pests: Aphids, pepper weevil, flea beetles, hornworms
common_diseases: Bacterial spot, anthracnose, blossom end rot, pepper mosaic virus

name: Banana Pepper 'Sweet Banana'
description: The perfect mild pepper for gardeners who love the flavor of peppers without any heat whatsoever. Sweet Banana peppers are incredibly productive, producing loads of pale yellow, curved pods that add beautiful color and sweet crunch to any dish. Easy to grow and harvest continuously throughout the season, they're ideal for pickling, fresh eating, and adding to pizza and sandwiches.
soil_type: Well-drained fertile soil with good organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Transplant when soil temperature reaches 65°F consistently.
shape: Long, curved, tapered with pointed tip
flavor_profile: Sweet and mild with no heat, crisp texture
culinary_uses: Pickling, fresh eating, pizza toppings, sandwiches, salads, stuffing
disease_resistance: Good resistance to common pepper diseases
common_pests: Aphids, flea beetles, pepper weevil, cutworms
common_diseases: Bacterial spot, blossom end rot, pepper mosaic virus, anthracnose

name: Sweet Pepper 'Cubanelle'
description: Often called the 'Italian Frying Pepper,' this sweet, thin-walled variety is prized for its exceptional flavor and tender texture that makes it perfect for quick cooking. Popular in Caribbean and Italian cuisine, Cubanelle peppers offer a mild, sweet taste with just a hint of heat that appeals to all palates. Their elongated shape and vibrant color make them as beautiful in the garden as they are delicious on the plate.
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with good organic matter
sowing_method: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Transplant outdoors after soil warms to 60°F and night temperatures stay above 50°F.
color: Light green to yellow-green, ripening to red
shape: Long, tapered, slightly curved with thin walls
flavor_profile: Very mild and sweet with almost no heat (0-1,000 Scoville), crisp when fresh
culinary_uses: Frying, sautéing, stuffing, salads, sandwiches, Italian and Caribbean dishes
disease_resistance: Moderate resistance to common pepper diseases
common_pests: Aphids, pepper weevil, European corn borer, flea beetles
common_diseases: Bacterial spot, phytophthora blight, pepper mottle virus

name: Sweet Pepper 'California Wonder'
description: The gold standard for home garden bell peppers since 1928, this reliable heirloom produces thick-walled, blocky peppers that are perfect for stuffing, grilling, or eating fresh. Known for consistent production and excellent disease resistance, it's the variety that taught generations of gardeners how to grow peppers successfully. The classic choice that never goes out of style.
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile loam
sowing_method: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Transplant when soil reaches 60°F and night temperatures stay above 50°F.
shape: Blocky, four-lobed bell shape with thick walls
flavor_profile: Sweet, crisp, no heat (0 Scoville), classic bell pepper flavor
culinary_uses: Stuffed peppers, stir-fries, salads, grilling, roasting, fresh eating
disease_resistance: Good resistance to tobacco mosaic virus
common_pests: Aphids, pepper hornworms, flea beetles, cutworms
common_diseases: Bacterial spot, blossom end rot, anthracnose

name: Sweet Italian Pepper 'Marconi Rosso'
description: An exceptional Italian heirloom frying pepper renowned for its incredible sweetness and tender flesh when cooked. These long, tapered peppers start green and ripen to a gorgeous deep red, developing an almost candy-like sweetness that makes them irresistible grilled, roasted, or sautéed. A favorite among Italian-American gardeners and chefs who prize authentic flavors in their cooking.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Transplant when soil temperature reaches 65°F consistently.
shape: Long, tapered, slightly curved with thick walls
flavor_profile: Exceptionally sweet with no heat, fruity undertones
culinary_uses: Frying, roasting, grilling, stuffing, Italian dishes, sandwiches, preserved in oil
disease_resistance: Moderate resistance to common pepper diseases
common_pests: Aphids, pepper maggot, European corn borer, thrips
common_diseases: Bacterial leaf spot, verticillium wilt, tobacco mosaic virus

name: Purple Beauty Bell Pepper
description: A stunning ornamental and edible bell pepper that produces gorgeous deep purple fruits that eventually ripen to red if left on the plant. This eye-catching variety combines the classic sweet bell pepper flavor with incredible visual appeal, making it perfect for gardeners who want both beauty and function in their vegetable gardens. The compact plants are ideal for containers and add dramatic color to any garden space.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with good organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost date. Transplant when soil temperature stays above 60°F.
shape: Classic blocky bell pepper shape with thick walls
flavor_profile: Sweet and mild, typical bell pepper flavor with no heat
culinary_uses: Fresh eating, salads, stuffing, stir-fries, ornamental gardens, colorful dishes
disease_resistance: Good hybrid vigor with resistance to tobacco mosaic virus
common_pests: Aphids, pepper weevil, flea beetles, cutworms
common_diseases: Bacterial leaf spot, pepper mosaic virus, blossom end rot

name: Black Seeded Simpson
description: An early producer of light green, curled, tender leaves. MT0-30.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with organic matter
sowing_method: Direct sow seeds 1/4 inch deep, 2-3 weeks before last frost. Succession plant every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest.
shape: Loose-leaf with deeply frilled, curled leaves
flavor_profile: Mild, sweet, and tender with no bitterness
culinary_uses: Salads, sandwiches, wraps, garnish. Excellent for cut-and-come-again harvesting.
disease_resistance: Good tolerance to heat stress and some resistance to tipburn
common_pests: Aphids, flea beetles, slugs, cutworms
common_diseases: Downy mildew, lettuce drop, tipburn, bolting in hot weather

name: Buttercrunch
description: Johnny's produces Buttercrunch lettuce using the original stock seed from Cornell University. Forms a small, open but tightly bunched, 6" rosette that is fan-shaped rather than round. Dark green leaves and small compact hearts that blanch to an appetizing yellow color. Crisp and sweet. MT0-30.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with high organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost or direct sow in early spring. Plant seeds 1/4 inch deep in cool, moist soil.
color: Dark green outer leaves with pale yellow-green hearts
shape: Compact butterhead with loose rosette formation
flavor_profile: Sweet, buttery, and crisp with a delicate, nutty finish
culinary_uses: Gourmet salads, lettuce cups, sandwiches, garnish. Perfect for fine dining presentations.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to tipburn and moderate bolt resistance
common_pests: Aphids, leafminers, slugs, flea beetles
common_diseases: Downy mildew, bottom rot, tipburn, bolting in heat

name: Romaine Cos
description: The classic upright lettuce that forms tall, sturdy heads of dark green leaves with prominent white ribs and exceptional crunch. This traditional variety has been cultivated for over 2,000 years and remains the gold standard for Caesar salads and Mediterranean cuisine. Its robust structure and intense flavor make it indispensable for gardeners who want restaurant-quality lettuce at home.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, deep watering preferred
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with good organic matter
sowing_method: Direct sow 1/4 inch deep in early spring or start indoors. Thin seedlings to proper spacing when 2 inches tall.
color: Dark green with prominent white ribs
shape: Upright, elongated heads with thick, sturdy leaves
flavor_profile: Crisp, slightly bitter, robust with mineral undertones
culinary_uses: Caesar salad, grilling, wraps, Mediterranean dishes. Essential for authentic Caesar preparations.
disease_resistance: Moderate resistance to tipburn, susceptible to bottom rot in wet conditions
common_pests: Aphids, leafminers, cutworms, flea beetles
common_diseases: Downy mildew, bottom rot, tipburn, bacterial leaf spot

name: Red Sails
description: Attractive, ruffled, fringed leaves of deep burgundy red over green. AAS Winner. MT0-30.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with organic amendments
sowing_method: Direct sow seeds 1/4 inch deep from early spring through summer. Succession plant every 2-3 weeks for continuous color.
color: Green centers with deep red-burgundy leaf edges
shape: Loose-leaf with deeply frilled, oak-like leaves
flavor_profile: Mild, sweet flavor with tender texture and no bitterness
culinary_uses: Colorful salad mixes, garnish, mesclun blends. Adds visual drama to any dish.
disease_resistance: Excellent heat tolerance and bolt resistance, moderate disease resistance
common_pests: Aphids, flea beetles, slugs, leafminers
common_diseases: Downy mildew, tipburn, lettuce drop in wet conditions

name: Iceberg
description: The quintessential American head lettuce that forms tight, dense heads of crisp, pale green leaves with unmatched crunch and refreshing flavor. While challenging to grow perfectly, successful heads reward gardeners with the ultimate salad lettuce that stays fresh for weeks and provides that signature satisfying crunch. This variety requires patience and proper timing but delivers restaurant-quality results when grown correctly.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, consistent deep watering
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with excellent organic content
growing_season: Cool season, requires cool nights for heading
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Transplant when soil is consistently cool. Direct seeding often fails to form proper heads.
color: Pale green to white interior with light green outer leaves
shape: Dense, compact round heads with tightly wrapped leaves
flavor_profile: Mild, crisp, refreshing with high water content and clean finish
culinary_uses: Classic salads, sandwiches, tacos, coleslaw substitute. The standard for crisp lettuce applications.
disease_resistance: Susceptible to tipburn and bottom rot, requires cool conditions to prevent bolting
common_pests: Aphids, cutworms, wireworms, flea beetles
common_diseases: Tipburn, bottom rot, downy mildew, premature bolting in heat

name: Great Lakes
description: A classic crisphead lettuce that delivers the satisfying crunch of iceberg but with better heat tolerance and garden performance. This reliable variety forms dense, well-blanched heads with crisp, sweet leaves that stay fresh longer than most lettuce types. Perfect for gardeners who want that classic lettuce experience without the challenges of growing true iceberg varieties.

name: Oak Leaf
description: An elegant loose-leaf lettuce with distinctive deeply-lobed leaves that resemble oak tree foliage, adding visual interest to both garden and salad bowl. This heat-tolerant variety offers exceptional flavor with tender, buttery leaves that never become bitter, making it perfect for continuous harvest throughout the growing season. The unique leaf shape and reliable performance make it a favorite among both novice and experienced gardeners.

description: A uniform strain of an old French variety renowned for its buttery texture and sweet flavor. Exceptionally quick to close and blanch internal leaves. Heavily savoyed leaf. Pairs well with Rosaine and Cegolaine. Does not hold in the field as long as Newham. MT0-30. Also available with NOP-compliant pelleting.

This compact variety produces dense heads packed with crispy, uniform leaves that maintain excellent texture and freshness longer than traditional lettuce types. Perfect for busy gardeners and commercial growers who want maximum efficiency and consistent results.

name: Red Velvet
description: A stunning loose-leaf variety that brings dramatic burgundy-red color to the garden and gourmet appeal to the table with its deeply ruffled, almost frilly leaves. This heat-tolerant beauty maintains its vibrant coloration even in warm weather while delivering exceptional flavor with tender, sweet leaves that add both visual impact and culinary excellence to any salad mix. The combination of ornamental beauty and outstanding performance makes it a standout choice for edible landscaping.

description: A reliable, fast-growing loose-leaf lettuce that's perfect for beginners and continuous harvesting. The tender, ruffled green leaves provide mild, sweet flavor and can be harvested leaf by leaf for weeks of fresh salads. This heat-tolerant variety is ideal for succession planting throughout the growing season.

name: Batavia
description: Batavia is a crinkled-leaf heirloom lettuce with a distinctive ruffled appearance and tender, frilly foliage that ranges from light to medium green. Maturing in approximately 47 days, this variety bridges butterhead and leaf lettuce characteristics, forming a loose head while maintaining the delicate texture of loose-leaf types. Its crisp, sweet flavor with nutty undertones and subtle mineral complexity makes it ideal for fresh salads and gourmet presentations. The crinkled leaves add visual appeal and pleasant texture contrast. Batavia thrives in cool-season gardens with full sun to partial shade and prefers rich, well-drained loam, making it accessible for both novice and experienced growers.

The small, compact heads form perfect individual serving sizes with butter-soft texture that melts in your mouth. This gourmet variety is favored by chefs and home gardeners who appreciate premium salad quality.

description: A revolutionary multi-leaf lettuce that produces 16-20 individual leaves from a single cut, making harvest incredibly efficient and waste-free. The tender, red-tinged butterhead-type leaves offer premium texture and sweet flavor while the innovative breeding ensures every leaf is perfectly sized for salads. This modern variety combines convenience with gourmet quality.

name: Arugula
description: Arugula is a fast-growing leafy green with slender, deeply lobed leaves that mature in just 10-15 days. This heirloom variety thrives in cool seasons and prefers full sun to partial shade. The distinctive peppery, nutty flavor with a slight bitterness and pungent kick makes it ideal for fresh salads, garnishes, and cooked dishes. Arugula's rapid maturity and ease of cultivation—combined with its bold, complex taste—distinguish it from milder lettuce varieties. It tolerates cool weather well and can be succession-planted for continuous harvests throughout the growing season.

name: Spinach
description: Spinach is a nutrient-dense leafy green with tender, deep green leaves that develop characteristic slight crinkles as they mature. Ready to harvest in approximately 25 days, this hybrid variety transitions from a mild, slightly sweet flavor when young to a more complex, mineral-rich taste with age. It thrives in cool seasons and performs well in full sun to partial shade conditions. Spinach is versatile in the kitchen—equally excellent fresh in salads when young or cooked in mature form. Its rapid growth and ease of cultivation make it ideal for beginner gardeners seeking quick, reliable harvests.

name: Mâche (Corn Salad)
description: This versatile, vigorous, mildew-resistant variety is excellent at a time of year when greens become scarce. Long, oval, glossy green leaves form tight rosettes. Mild, slightly nutty flavor also reminiscent of roses. Also known as mâche, lamb's lettuce, and corn salad. Unsized seed.

name: Genovese Basil
description: Authentic flavor and appearance. Tall and relatively slow to bolt with large dark green leaves about 3" long. This common strain of Genovese basil can present some variability in leaf shape and plant size. While quite suitable for field and garden, we recommend using a more modern and more uniform variety for greenhouse, container, or hydroponic production, such as Genovese Compact Improved, Aroma 2, Nufar, Dolly, or the Prospera® series. Ht. 24-30".Edible Flowers: Use the flowers in any recipe that calls for basil, or to garnish drinks, salads, soups, pasta, and desserts. Flavor is of intense basil.Also available in organic raw and pelleted seed.

name: Flat-Leaf Parsley
description: Also known as Italian parsley, this variety offers superior flavor compared to curly parsley with its clean, bright taste that doesn't overpower dishes. The flat, deeply-cut leaves are easier to chop and provide a fresh, grassy flavor that's essential in Mediterranean cooking. This hardy biennial is incredibly productive and continues growing through light frosts, making it a kitchen garden staple.

name: Common Thyme
description: Common Thyme is a compact, woody perennial herb with tiny, narrow green leaves and delicate pink or purple flowers. Reaching maturity in 90-95 days, it becomes a robust ground cover perfect for edging and containers. This Mediterranean native thrives in poor, well-drained soil and is remarkably cold-hardy. Its earthy, minty flavor with warm, pungent undertones makes it essential for cooking—particularly valued in French cuisine and Mediterranean dishes. More cold-tolerant than most culinary herbs, Common Thyme delivers consistent flavor year-round and rarely suffers from serious pest issues.

description: Sweet Basil is a tender annual herb prized for its vibrant green leaves and distinctive aromatic flavor. This heirloom variety reaches harvest maturity in approximately 74 days, producing compact, bushy plants ideal for containers or garden beds. Its sweet, clove-forward taste with subtle anise undertones makes it the quintessential choice for Italian cuisine, fresh pestos, and culinary applications. Unlike spicier basil varieties, Sweet Basil's delicate, complex flavor profile and ease of cultivation have made it a kitchen garden staple for centuries.

The plant produces thin, lacy stems bearing distinctive serrated leaves with a bright, citrusy flavor profile that carries subtle soapy notes and fresh herbal undertones. Cilantro thrives in full sun to partial shade and prefers well-drained, fertile soil. As a quick-maturing heirloom variety, it's ideal for succession planting throughout the growing season. description: Chocolate Mint is a distinctive heirloom herb variety that matures in 65-75 days, featuring aromatic green foliage with soft, velvety texture. This unique mint hybrid stands out for its exceptional flavor profile: a refreshing cool mint taste with prominent chocolate undertones and a subtle sweet finish, making it ideal for both culinary applications and specialty beverages. Despite its rich flavor complexity, Chocolate Mint remains easy to grow, thriving in full sun with well-drained, moist soil. The plant tolerates heavy clay conditions well, making it adaptable to various garden settings.

Unlike compact basil varieties, its generous leaf size reduces preparation time while delivering the authentic, complex flavor profile that defines traditional Italian cooking.

description: A charming miniature basil that forms perfect little mounds of tiny, intensely flavored leaves - ideal for container gardens and small spaces. This easy-to-grow perennial reaches maturity in 120-150 days, producing delicate flowers that attract pollinators. The leaves deliver authentic thyme flavor—earthy, minty, and subtly floral—making it ideal for culinary applications, particularly Mediterranean dishes and herbal infusions. Hardy and drought-tolerant, Silver Thyme thrives in well-drained, sandy, or rocky soil with minimal care, distinguishing it through superior flavor complexity compared to common thyme varieties.

These beautiful purple-black beans produce abundantly and are prized for their rich, meaty texture and deep, complex flavor that improves with cooking. name: German Giant Radish
description: A massive white radish that can grow to impressive sizes while maintaining surprisingly mild flavor and crisp texture. Unlike typical small radishes, German Giant becomes milder and sweeter as it grows larger, making it perfect for cooking applications. This unique variety bridges the gap between European radishes and Asian daikon types.
water_requirement: 1 inch per week, consistent moisture to prevent splitting
soil_type: Deep, loose, fertile soil with good drainage
sowing_method: Direct sow seeds 1/2 inch deep in spring or fall. Can be succession planted every 2 weeks in cool weather.
flavor_profile: Mild, sweet, crisp with less bite than small radishes
culinary_uses: Fresh eating, salads, roasting, stir-frying, braising, pickling. Excellent cooked like turnips.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to clubroot and black rot
common_pests: Flea beetles, cabbage root maggot, aphids
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, downy mildew

name: Red Norland Potato
description: The gold standard for early-season red potatoes, beloved by home gardeners for its reliability and excellent flavor. These smooth-skinned beauties are ready to harvest as delicious new potatoes in just 60 days, or left to mature for storage. Their waxy texture and thin, edible skins make them perfect for boiling, steaming, and potato salads.
water_requirement: 1-2 inches per week, reduce watering as harvest approaches
soil_type: Loose, well-drained, slightly acidic soil rich in organic matter
sowing_method: Plant seed potatoes 4 inches deep, 2 weeks before last frost. Hill soil around plants as they grow to prevent greening.
flavor_profile: Mild, buttery, slightly sweet with waxy texture
culinary_uses: Boiling, steaming, roasting, potato salad, new potatoes. Thin skin doesn't require peeling.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to scab and moderate resistance to late blight
common_pests: Colorado potato beetle, wireworms, potato flea beetle
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, potato scab, bacterial soft rot

name: Pontiac Red Potato
description: A reliable mid-season potato variety beloved for its attractive red skin and pure white flesh that holds its shape beautifully when cooked. Pontiac produces excellent yields of medium to large tubers and shows good resistance to common potato diseases. This versatile variety is perfect for boiling, baking, and making colorful potato salads.
water_requirement: 1-2 inches per week, reduce watering 2 weeks before harvest
soil_type: Loose, well-drained soil with good organic matter
sowing_method: Plant seed potatoes 2-3 weeks before last frost date. Cut pieces should have 2-3 eyes. Hill soil around plants as they grow.
flavor_profile: Mild, earthy flavor with creamy texture
culinary_uses: Boiling, baking, roasting, potato salad, mashing. Holds shape well when cooked.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to scab and some virus strains
common_pests: Colorado potato beetle, aphids, wireworms, flea beetles
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, potato scab, blackleg

name: German Butterball Potato
description: An outstanding heirloom potato variety that delivers incredibly rich, buttery flavor in smooth-textured yellow flesh. This late-season variety produces excellent yields of medium-sized tubers with buff-colored skin and stores exceptionally well through winter. German Butterball is considered one of the best-tasting potatoes available to home gardeners.
water_requirement: 1-2 inches per week, consistent moisture during tuber development
soil_type: Deep, loose, well-drained soil with high organic matter
sowing_method: Plant seed potatoes after soil temperature reaches 45°F. Cut pieces should cure 24-48 hours before planting. Hill regularly.
color: Buff/tan skin with deep yellow flesh
flavor_profile: Rich, buttery flavor with dense, creamy texture
culinary_uses: Baking, mashing, roasting, frying. Excellent for gourmet preparations and winter storage.
disease_resistance: Moderate disease resistance, typical of heirloom varieties
common_pests: Colorado potato beetle, aphids, potato tuberworm
common_diseases: Late blight, early blight, potato scab

name: Scarlet Queen Turnip
description: Scarlet Queen is a heirloom turnip variety prized for its stunning deep red to crimson skin that stands out in the garden and kitchen. Maturing in just 37 days, this quick-growing root vegetable produces tender, globe-shaped roots with crisp white flesh. Unlike many turnips, Scarlet Queen delivers a distinctly sweet, mild flavor without bitter notes, making it excellent for both raw consumption in salads and cooked preparations. The vibrant skin color provides visual appeal while the tender texture remains consistent even when harvested at larger sizes. An easy-to-grow heirloom suitable for gardeners of all skill levels.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-8 hours)
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with good organic matter
sowing_method: Direct seed in early spring 2-3 weeks before last frost or in late summer for fall harvest. Thin seedlings to proper spacing.
color: Bright red skin with white flesh
flavor_profile: Sweet, mild turnip flavor without bitterness, crisp texture
culinary_uses: Fresh eating, salads, roasting, braising, pickling. Greens are also edible and nutritious.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to clubroot and turnip mosaic virus
common_pests: Flea beetles, aphids, root maggots, cabbage worms
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, downy mildew

name: Purple Carrot Cosmic Purple
description: A stunning heirloom carrot that brings vibrant color to your garden and plate with its deep purple exterior and bright orange core. This eye-catching variety delivers excellent sweet flavor while providing powerful antioxidants from its rich purple pigmentation. Perfect for gardeners who want to grow something truly unique that will amaze friends and family.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Deep, loose, sandy loam free of stones
sowing_method: Direct sow seeds 2-3 weeks before last frost. Sow 1/4 inch deep and thin seedlings when 2 inches tall.
color: Deep purple exterior with bright orange core
flavor_profile: Sweet and crisp with classic carrot flavor, slightly spicier than orange varieties
culinary_uses: Fresh eating, roasting, juicing, colorful salads, pickles. Loses some color when cooked.
disease_resistance: Good general disease resistance, moderate carrot fly resistance
common_pests: Carrot rust fly, wireworms, cutworms
common_diseases: Alternaria leaf blight, bacterial soft rot, cavity spot

name: Kennebec Potato
description: The ultimate all-purpose potato that excels at everything from fluffy baked potatoes to crispy French fries, making it a favorite among home gardeners and commercial growers alike. This reliable variety produces excellent yields of smooth, white-skinned potatoes with outstanding storage qualities. Known for its disease resistance and adaptability, Kennebec is perfect for gardeners seeking a dependable, versatile potato variety.
water_requirement: 1-2 inches per week, avoid overwatering near harvest
soil_type: Well-drained, loose, fertile soil with good organic matter
sowing_method: Plant seed potatoes 4 inches deep, 2 weeks before last frost. Hill soil around plants as they grow.
color: Light tan to white skin, white flesh
flavor_profile: Mild, classic potato flavor with fluffy, dry texture when cooked
culinary_uses: Excellent for baking, frying, mashing, roasting. Perfect for French fries and chips.
disease_resistance: Excellent resistance to late blight, good scab resistance, moderate virus resistance
common_pests: Colorado potato beetle, aphids, wireworms, flea beetles
common_diseases: Early blight, blackleg, common scab (mild)

name: Black Spanish Round Radish
description: An ancient heirloom winter radish prized for its striking black skin and crisp white flesh that delivers a bold, peppery punch perfect for adding excitement to winter meals. This hardy storage radish can be kept for months in proper conditions, making it invaluable for extending the harvest season. With its unique appearance and intense flavor, it's a conversation starter that brings old-world character to modern gardens.
soil_type: Well-drained, loose soil with good organic matter
sowing_method: Direct sow seeds 1/2 inch deep in late summer for fall harvest, 10-12 weeks before hard frost.
color: Black exterior skin, pure white flesh
flavor_profile: Very pungent and spicy, much hotter than spring radishes, with a sharp bite
culinary_uses: Excellent for pickling, winter soups, stir-fries, eaten raw in thin slices. Traditional in Spanish and German cuisine.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to clubroot, moderate resistance to black rot
common_pests: Flea beetles, cabbage root maggot, aphids
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, white rust

name: Touchon Carrot
description: A beloved French heirloom carrot renowned for its exceptional sweetness and crisp texture, often considered one of the best-tasting carrots available to home gardeners. This variety produces perfectly straight, smooth roots with little to no core, making every bite tender and flavorful. Touchon's reliable performance and gourmet quality have made it a favorite among gardeners who prioritize flavor over size.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Deep, loose, sandy loam free of stones and debris
sowing_method: Direct sow seeds 1/4 inch deep, 2-3 weeks before last frost. Successive plantings every 2-3 weeks.
shape: Cylindrical, blunt-ended Nantes type, very straight and smooth
flavor_profile: Exceptionally sweet with crisp texture, virtually coreless, tender throughout
culinary_uses: Perfect for fresh eating, juicing, cooking. Excellent for baby carrots when harvested young.
disease_resistance: Good general disease resistance, some tolerance to alternaria leaf blight
common_pests: Carrot rust fly, wireworms, aphids
common_diseases: Alternaria leaf blight, bacterial soft rot, aster yellows

name: Calabrese Broccoli
description: The classic Italian heirloom that gave us the broccoli we know today, originating from the Calabria region. This traditional variety produces medium-sized blue-green heads with excellent flavor and reliable side shoot production after the main head is harvested. A must-grow for gardeners seeking authentic Italian flavor and continuous harvests.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with high organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost or direct sow in late summer for fall harvest. Transplant 2-3 weeks before last frost.
shape: Dense, dome-shaped central head with tight florets
flavor_profile: Classic broccoli flavor, sweet and nutty with slight bitterness
culinary_uses: Steaming, roasting, stir-fries, raw in salads, blanching and freezing
disease_resistance: Moderate resistance to clubroot and black rot
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage loopers
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, downy mildew, bacterial soft rot

name: Dwarf Blue Curled Kale
scientific_name: Brassica oleracea var. acephala 'Dwarf Blue Curled'
description: A compact heirloom kale variety dating back to the 1860s, prized for its intensely curled blue-green leaves and sweet flavor that improves with frost. This space-saving variety is perfect for small gardens and containers while still providing abundant harvests of tender, flavorful leaves. The attractive, heavily ruffled foliage also makes it an excellent ornamental edible.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with high organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost or direct sow in late summer for fall harvest. Transplant 2-4 weeks before last frost.
color: Blue-green with purple tinges in cold weather
shape: Heavily curled and ruffled leaves, compact rosette
flavor_profile: Sweet and mild, becoming sweeter after frost exposure
culinary_uses: Salads (young leaves), sautéing, soups, smoothies, chips, braising
disease_resistance: Good cold tolerance, moderate disease resistance
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage loopers
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, downy mildew

name: Dinosaur Kale
description: Dinosaur Kale is a heirloom Brassica featuring distinctive bumpy, deeply textured dark green leaves that resemble dinosaur skin—the source of its charming name. Maturing in 125 days under full sun, this variety stands out for its remarkably sweet, nutty flavor with significantly less bitterness than curly kale varieties, making it exceptionally palatable both raw and cooked. The tender leaves are ideal for salads, smoothies, and sautéed dishes. Thriving in rich, well-drained soil amended with organic matter, Dinosaur Kale is an easy-to-grow variety perfect for both beginners and experienced gardeners.
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter
sowing_method: Direct seed 2-4 weeks before last spring frost or start indoors 4-6 weeks before transplanting. For fall harvest, sow 12-14 weeks before first fall frost.
color: Dark blue-green with prominent white veins
shape: Long, narrow, strap-like leaves with heavily textured surface
flavor_profile: Sweet, nutty flavor with less bitterness than curly kale varieties
culinary_uses: Excellent for sautéing, braising, soups, salads (massage raw leaves), smoothies, and traditional Italian dishes
disease_resistance: Good resistance to bolting and frost damage. Moderate resistance to common brassica diseases.
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage loopers
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, downy mildew, white rust

name: Copenhagen Market Cabbage
description: A classic early-maturing cabbage that's been a gardener favorite since 1909, prized for its reliability and compact growth habit. This Danish heirloom produces perfectly round, solid heads with crisp, sweet leaves that are ideal for fresh eating or quick cooking. Its ability to mature quickly while maintaining excellent quality makes it perfect for successive plantings.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, consistent moisture especially during head formation
soil_type: Rich, fertile, well-drained soil with high organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last spring frost. Transplant when 4-6 inches tall. For fall crop, direct seed or transplant 12-14 weeks before hard frost.
color: Light to medium green outer leaves with pale green interior
flavor_profile: Crisp texture with sweet, mild cabbage flavor
culinary_uses: Excellent for coleslaw, salads, stir-fries, stuffed cabbage, and light cooking. Good fresh storage variety.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to splitting and bolting. Moderate disease resistance typical of heirlooms.
common_pests: Cabbage worms, cutworms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage root maggots
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, fusarium yellows, downy mildew

name: Waltham 29 Broccoli
description: Developed at the University of Massachusetts, this cold-hardy broccoli variety was specifically bred to extend the growing season well into winter in northern climates. It produces medium-sized, deep blue-green heads followed by an abundance of tender side shoots that can be harvested for weeks. This reliable performer is perfect for gardeners wanting fresh broccoli through the fall and early winter months.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, consistent moisture especially during head development
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with high organic matter content
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last spring frost for spring crop. For fall harvest, start seeds indoors in mid-summer, 12-14 weeks before hard frost.
color: Deep blue-green heads with tight, compact florets
shape: Compact, dome-shaped central head with numerous side shoots
flavor_profile: Sweet, nutty flavor with excellent texture and minimal bitterness
culinary_uses: Excellent for steaming, roasting, stir-frying, and raw in salads. Both main heads and side shoots are delicious.
disease_resistance: Good cold tolerance and resistance to bolting. Moderate resistance to common broccoli diseases.
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage loopers
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, downy mildew, alternaria leaf spot

name: Burpee Hybrid Broccoli
description: A reliable hybrid broccoli that produces large, tight heads with excellent uniformity and heat tolerance. This variety is prized for its ability to produce substantial side shoots after the main head is harvested, extending the harvest season significantly.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with high organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost or direct sow 2-3 weeks before last frost. For fall harvest, start 12-14 weeks before first fall frost.
shape: Large, tight, dome-shaped heads with fine beads
flavor_profile: Mild, sweet broccoli flavor with tender stems
culinary_uses: Steaming, stir-frying, roasting, raw in salads, freezing
disease_resistance: Good resistance to downy mildew and black rot
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage loopers
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, downy mildew

name: Winterbor Kale
description: Plants are tall, with excellent yield and good cold hardiness. The ruffled blue-green leaves have an attractive curl. Vigorous, productive plants.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
water_requirement: 1 inch per week, drought tolerant once established
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with good organic content
sowing_method: Direct sow 10-12 weeks before first fall frost, or start indoors and transplant. Can also be sown in early spring 4-6 weeks before last frost.
color: Blue-green with purple tinting in cold weather
flavor_profile: Sweet, mild kale flavor, especially sweet after frost
culinary_uses: Salads, smoothies, sautéing, soups, kale chips, braising
disease_resistance: Excellent cold tolerance, resistant to bolting
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles
common_diseases: Black rot, clubroot, downy mildew

name: Early Flat Dutch Cabbage
scientific_name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata 'Early Flat Dutch'
description: A classic heirloom cabbage dating back to the 1840s, prized for its large, flattened heads that can weigh 10-15 pounds. This reliable variety produces solid, sweet heads with excellent storage qualities and is perfect for making sauerkraut or coleslaw.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, consistent moisture important
soil_type: Rich, well-drained, fertile soil with high organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last spring frost for summer harvest, or 12-14 weeks before first fall frost for fall harvest.
color: Light to medium green outer leaves, pale green interior
flavor_profile: Sweet, mild cabbage flavor with tender texture
culinary_uses: Coleslaw, sauerkraut, stuffed cabbage, soups, braising, fresh eating
disease_resistance: Moderate disease resistance, good storage qualities
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage root maggots
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, fusarium yellows

name: Cabbage 'Stonehead'
description: An award-winning hybrid that produces perfectly round, compact heads with exceptional storage quality. This reliable variety forms dense, 3-4 pound heads that resist splitting and maintain their quality in the garden longer than most cabbages. Stonehead's consistent performance and excellent flavor make it a top choice for home gardeners seeking reliability.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost for spring crop. Direct sow or transplant for fall crop 12-14 weeks before first hard frost.
color: Blue-green outer leaves with pale green interior
flavor_profile: Sweet, mild cabbage flavor with crisp, tender texture
culinary_uses: Coleslaw, sauerkraut, stir-fries, soups, steaming, raw salads, storage
disease_resistance: Good resistance to splitting and yellows disease
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cutworms, cabbage root maggot
common_diseases: Clubroot, black rot, fusarium yellows, downy mildew

name: Green Goliath Broccoli
description: A hybrid powerhouse that produces massive 6-8 inch heads on sturdy plants that tower over other broccoli varieties. Green Goliath lives up to its name with exceptional heat tolerance and the ability to produce substantial side shoots after the main head is harvested, extending your harvest season significantly.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost or direct sow 2-3 weeks before last frost. For fall crop, start 12-14 weeks before first fall frost.
shape: Large, tight, dome-shaped heads with fine beads
flavor_profile: Sweet, mild, and tender with no bitterness
culinary_uses: Steaming, stir-frying, roasting, fresh eating, freezing well for later use
disease_resistance: Good resistance to clubroot and downy mildew
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage loopers
common_diseases: Black rot, clubroot, downy mildew, white rust

name: Red Acre Cabbage
description: An early-maturing red cabbage that forms compact, baseball-sized heads perfect for small families and succession planting. This reliable variety produces gorgeous deep purple-red heads that hold their color beautifully when cooked and adds stunning visual appeal to any garden or plate.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with good organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost or direct sow 2-3 weeks before last frost. For fall crop, start 12-14 weeks before first fall frost.
flavor_profile: Mild, sweet flavor with tender, crisp texture
culinary_uses: Coleslaw, sauerkraut, braising, pickling, fresh salads, cooking retains beautiful color
disease_resistance: Good resistance to splitting and yellows
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage root maggots
common_diseases: Black rot, clubroot, fusarium yellows, downy mildew

name: Vates Dwarf Blue Curled Kale
scientific_name: Brassica oleracea var. acephala 'Vates Dwarf Blue Curled'
description: A compact, cold-hardy kale variety that was specifically bred for both home gardens and commercial production, winning an AAS award for its reliability. The tightly curled, blue-green leaves pack incredible nutrition into a space-saving plant that actually improves in flavor after frost touches the leaves.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Well-drained soil, tolerates poor soils better than most brassicas
sowing_method: Direct sow 2-4 weeks before last frost for spring crop. For fall crop, sow 10-12 weeks before first fall frost.
shape: Deeply curled and ruffled leaves, compact rosette form
flavor_profile: Mild, sweet flavor that becomes sweeter after frost exposure
culinary_uses: Smoothies, sautéing, kale chips, soups, salads when young and tender
disease_resistance: Excellent cold tolerance, good resistance to bolting
common_pests: Aphids, cabbage worms, flea beetles
common_diseases: Black rot, downy mildew, white rust

name: Purple Sprouting Broccoli 'Early Purple Sprouting'
scientific_name: Brassica oleracea var. italica 'Early Purple Sprouting'
description: A stunning heirloom variety that produces abundant purple flower heads over an extended harvest period. Unlike regular broccoli, this cold-hardy gem overwinters and provides fresh spears when little else is growing in the garden. The purple heads turn green when cooked and offer a sweet, nutty flavor that's considered superior to regular broccoli.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter
sowing_method: Start seeds indoors in late spring or direct sow in early summer for overwintering harvest. Plant out in midsummer.
color: Deep purple heads that turn green when cooked
size: Small to medium heads, 2-4 inches across
shape: Loose, sprouting clusters rather than tight heads
flavor_profile: Sweet, nutty, and tender with less bitterness than regular broccoli
culinary_uses: Steam, stir-fry, roast, or eat raw. Excellent in pasta dishes and grain bowls. Entire stem and leaves are edible.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to cold weather diseases, moderate clubroot tolerance
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, cabbage root fly
common_diseases: Clubroot, downy mildew, black rot, white rust

name: Cabbage 'Red Express'
description: A compact, early-maturing hybrid that produces perfectly round, deep red-purple heads in just 76 days. This space-saving variety is ideal for small gardens and containers while delivering the crisp texture and peppery-sweet flavor that makes red cabbage a kitchen favorite. The uniform heads resist splitting and store exceptionally well.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
soil_type: Rich, well-drained soil with good organic content
sowing_method: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost or direct sow 2-3 weeks before last frost date. Can succession plant for fall harvest.
flavor_profile: Crisp and crunchy with mild peppery-sweet flavor, less bitter than green cabbage
culinary_uses: Perfect for coleslaw, braising, pickling, and fermentation. Adds color to stir-fries and salads. Excellent for sauerkraut.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to fusarium yellows and black rot
common_pests: Cabbage worms, cutworms, aphids, flea beetles
common_diseases: Clubroot, black leg, downy mildew, white rust

name: Kale 'Winterbor F1'
description: The ultimate winter kale that actually improves in flavor after frost exposure, becoming sweeter and more tender. This vigorous hybrid produces masses of deeply curled, blue-green leaves that can withstand temperatures down to 10°F while continuing to grow. It's the go-to variety for gardeners wanting fresh greens throughout winter.
sun_requirement: Full sun to partial shade (4-6+ hours)
water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, drought tolerant once established
soil_type: Well-drained soil, tolerates poor soils better than most brassicas
sowing_method: Direct sow or transplant from early spring through late summer. For winter harvest, plant 10-12 weeks before first hard frost.
color: Blue-green with purple stems in cold weather
flavor_profile: Sweet and mild, especially after frost. Less bitter than many kale varieties.
culinary_uses: Excellent for smoothies, soups, chips, sautéing, and salads when massaged. Perfect for winter stews and braises.
disease_resistance: Excellent cold tolerance, good resistance to downy mildew
common_pests: Cabbage worms, aphids, flea beetles, leaf miners
common_diseases: Downy mildew, black rot, white rust, clubroot

name: Ailsa Craig Sweet Onion
description: A legendary exhibition onion variety from Scotland that can grow to enormous sizes while maintaining sweet, mild flavor. This pale yellow globe onion is famous for winning competitions and producing bulbs that can weigh 2-3 pounds when grown with proper care. Despite its impressive size, Ailsa Craig maintains excellent eating quality and stores reasonably well.
water_requirement: 1 inch per week, consistent moisture during bulb development
soil_type: Rich, well-drained loam with high organic content
sowing_method: Start seeds indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost. Transplant when soil can be worked and plants are pencil-thick.
color: Pale yellow to golden skin with white flesh
flavor_profile: Sweet and mild with low sulfur content
culinary_uses: Excellent for fresh eating, salads, sandwiches, light cooking. Too mild for strong flavoring applications.
disease_resistance: Moderate resistance to pink root and fusarium basal rot
common_pests: Onion maggot, thrips, aphids, cutworms
common_diseases: Downy mildew, purple blotch, neck rot, pink root

name: Red Burgundy Onion
description: A stunning deep red storage onion that combines beautiful color with excellent keeping qualities and robust flavor. The dark burgundy skin and purple-tinged white flesh make this variety as ornamental as it is functional in the kitchen. Red Burgundy stores for 6-8 months when properly cured, making it ideal for gardeners who want year-round homegrown onions.
water_requirement: 1 inch per week, reduce watering 3 weeks before harvest
soil_type: Well-drained sandy loam, avoid heavy clay
sowing_method: Direct sow in early spring or start indoors 8-10 weeks before transplanting. Plant sets in early spring.
color: Deep burgundy red skin with purple-tinged white flesh
flavor_profile: Sharp, pungent flavor that mellows when cooked
culinary_uses: Excellent for cooking, grilling, pickling, and fresh use. Beautiful in salads and as garnish.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to pink root and fusarium basal rot
common_pests: Onion thrips, onion maggot, aphids
common_diseases: Downy mildew, purple blotch, bacterial soft rot

name: Elephant Garlic
description: Despite its name, Elephant Garlic is actually more closely related to leeks than true garlic, producing massive bulbs that can weigh up to one pound each. The flavor is much milder and sweeter than regular garlic, making it perfect for roasting whole or for those who want garlic flavor without the bite. Each enormous clove can be as large as a regular garlic bulb.
water_requirement: 1 inch per week during active growth, stop watering when leaves begin to yellow
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with good organic content
growing_season: Plant in fall for summer harvest
sowing_method: Plant cloves 4-6 inches deep in fall, 4-6 weeks before ground freezes. Pointed end up, blunt end down.
color: White to cream colored bulbs and cloves
size: 3-5 inch diameter bulbs, individual cloves 1-2 inches
shape: Large round bulbs with 4-6 huge cloves
flavor_profile: Mild, sweet garlic flavor, much less pungent than regular garlic
culinary_uses: Excellent roasted whole, grilled, or used fresh. Perfect for those who find regular garlic too strong.
disease_resistance: Generally disease resistant, more robust than regular garlic
common_pests: Aphids, thrips, onion maggot
common_diseases: White rot, fusarium basal rot, rust

name: Yellow Granex Onion
description: The authentic sweet onion that made Georgia's Vidalia region famous, Yellow Granex produces large, globe-shaped bulbs with exceptionally mild, sweet flavor. These golden beauties are so gentle they can be eaten like apples when grown in the right conditions. Perfect for gardeners wanting to grow their own version of premium sweet onions.
soil_type: Well-drained, fertile soil with high organic matter
sowing_method: Start seeds indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost, or plant sets/transplants in early spring when soil is workable.
color: Golden yellow skin with white flesh
flavor_profile: Exceptionally sweet and mild with very little sulfur bite
culinary_uses: Perfect for fresh eating, grilling, caramelizing, and salads. Not suitable for long-term storage.
disease_resistance: Good resistance to pink root and fusarium basal rot
common_pests: Onion thrips, onion maggots, cutworms
common_diseases: Downy mildew, purple blotch, neck rot

name: Copra Onion
description: The gold standard for long-storage onions, Copra delivers outstanding keeping quality with bulbs storing 8-12 months when properly cured. name: Walla Walla Sweet Onion
description: Juicy, sweet, regional favorite. SPRING PLANTING: Walla Walla may be spring planted using seeds or plants in colder regions where winter survival is hit or miss. It is not as big or sweet as the wintered-over crop, but still milder and juicier than others from spring planting. Nice as a "green top" onion. Not for storage. Adaptation: 35-55° latitude. Also offered organic, and as plants.

Delicate purple-pink pompom flowers appear in spring, adding ornamental appeal. Ready to harvest at 75-85 days from seed, though established plants provide year-round cutting. This hardy heirloom offers mild, delicate onion flavor with subtle sharpness, making it ideal for finishing dishes, garnishing soups, and creaming into sauces. description: Shanks bulk up quickly by mid-early season and resist bulbing for easy stripping. Performs well across the US and maintains high quality, even at a large size. An easy replacement for Jumper, which was discontinued by our supplier. Primed seed.

name: Katinka
description: Upright, tall plants make Katinka easy to harvest. Dark green curled leaves with a uniform canopy. Suitable for field or container production. Mild and pleasant parsley flavor. Katinka is very similar to Wega with the primary difference being that Katinka is taller for optimal bunch harvest and productivity in the field. Curled-leaf type. Ht. 14-20".

name: Topit

name: Summer Breeze Cherry Blossom
description: These gorgeous, everbearing, deep pink flowers are semidouble and put on a good show from midsummer to frost. No need for deadheading - this variety will continue to bloom even while it sets fruit. Let the flowers go by and enjoy bright red berries a few weeks later. Few runners. May overwinter with some pampering. Suitable for both container and in-ground growing. 10-12" plant with 1 1/2" flowers. Grows best in Zones 3-10.Edible Flowers: Mildly strawberry flavored blooms make for a tasty garnish.

name: Kapoor Tulsi (Holy Basil)
description: Compact but very full, attractive plants. Mild spicy aroma with hints of sweetness. Faster growing than green holy basil, and its purple flowers also make it a nice beneficial and/or ornamental. For teas, culinary, and medicinal use. Appears to have some resistance to downy mildew in our trials. Also known as "Spice Basil" and often referred to as Ocimum sanctum, although sanctum is not botanically correct. Ht. 12-18".
